newsitem.title: USA: Telephone and Data unit to boost spending.
newsitem.headline: Telephone and Data unit to boost spending.

text.p: Telephone and Data Systems Inc said Wednesday its wholly owned TDS Telecommunications Corp unit plans to invest about $130 million in capital equipment in 1997 to continue its ongoing service improvement programs.
In 1996, TDS invested about $110 million to $115 million in capital equipment, a spokeswoman said.

U.S. Cellular Corp, which is 80.6 percent owned by Telephone and Data, will invest about $300 million in capital equipment and business systems upgrades during 1997. American Paging Inc, its 82.3 percent owned unit, plans to invest about $35 million in 1997 in its paging operations.
In 1996, U.S. Cellular spent about $220 million, a spokesman said. American Paging's 1996 investments totaled about $29.0 million.
Earlier, Telephone and Data reported fourth quarter earnings of $0.19 a share, including $0.01 in gains from asset sales, down from year-ago earnings of $0.26 including $0.02 in gains.
Telephone and Data said its results reflected strong growth at U.S. Cellular, offset by personal communications services (PCS) development costs.

Aerial Communications Inc, its 82.3 percent owned unit, reported a loss of $0.20 a share, compared with a year-ago loss of $0.07. Aerial is in the process of launching PCS services in six major trading areas.
U.S. Cellular earned $0.13 a share in the fourth quarter, including $0.01 in gains, down from $0.23 a year ago, which included $0.07 in gains.

"Fourth quarter operating results include the effects of increased marketing costs primarily because we exceeded our expectations for net customer activations during the quarter and reached our revised penetration target for the year," H. Donald Nelson, president of U.S. Cellular, said in a statement.
American Paging had a loss of $0.66 a share, compared with a year-ago loss of $0.20, which the company said was disappointing, but in line with expectations.

"It is our goal in 1997 to significantly reduce our overall cost of service," Terrence Sullivan, American Paging president, said in a statement. "We have over the past quarter developed plans to migrate our customer base from the 19 frequencies and 43 networks we currently operate to no more than three frequencies and six networks."
